title: Widening the target on the same NQ breakout made 331% instead of 203% with a smaller drawdown
author: person-person12
selftext:
Cut your losses short and let your winners run is in every course and every thread in here, and i had never seen it tested on one set of rules. So i ran it both ways, and the only thing different between the two runs is where the target sits.

20 candle high breakout on NQ, 15 minute candles, long only, 1 ATR stop, entries between 09:30 and 15:45 ET, flat at 15:55. May 2016 to March 2026, 50k account, one contract. Commission at $2.50 a contract a side and half a tick of slippage, charged on both ends of every trade. Same code in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) for both runs.

**2 ATR target:** +202.52%, 40.92% of 3,050 trades won, profit factor 1.11, worst drawdown 24.26%.

**4 ATR target:** +330.84%, 34.26% of 2,452 trades won, profit factor 1.21, worst drawdown 20.31%.

The win rate dropped almost 7 points and the return went up by 128. **The wider target also drew less down**, which is the part i wasnt expecting, since the usual argument against a far target is that youre handing back open profit on the way to it.

Worth naming the trade counts before somebody reads them as a bug. The 4 ATR version took 598 fewer trades over the exact same candles. A position reaching for a target twice as far away sits open longer, and while its open the next breakout cant be entered, so moving the target out is filtering the entries as well as changing the exit. Some of that 128 point gap is trades the 2 ATR version took and the 4 ATR version never saw.
